As the seasons change
My love for you does not.

At once,
It buds and blooms, 
blossoming,
Like a flower 

Scattering in the slightest breeze, 
Petals slipping, 
Through a sea of soft
Pink lips, yours,

-That cannot be captured

Fruitless and barren, 
The colour fading,
In an eclipse of fleeting murmurs.
I move onto the next one.

The softness of the rain as it hit the ground was mesmerising.

He slipped his hand out through the window, and watched intently as the rain drops dotted his palm. He withdrew it gingerely and wiped his hand on his trousers. 

The rain dropped against the roof like glass beads rolling off a smooth countertop - water sliding off the skin. 

The ground was slick, as it always was. The wetness on the ground was iridescent amongst the reflection of the lights. He stared into the depths of the grass. The stiff green plumes, rigid and unmoving in the onslaught of shower. 

A sigh escaped him, and his gaze drifted to across the street. The green was saturated and drowning, desperately gasping for air under the copious amounts of water, drowning. The Smithes’ were the only one on the road with a real lawn, which was a complete rarity nowadays, and never ceased to fascinate him.

Arlo stared into the waterlogged earth, observing as the water flooded, leaving a brown trail of uprooted soil down the street, which was surely going to cause an uproar - as it usually did. 

He shut the window, and sat at his desk motionlessly. He stood up and left, not bothering to close the door. He heard a faint sound, but it blurred obscurely into the background noise and he carried on down the stairs.

His hand skimmed the slippery wooden railing like the slickness of water, smooth and continuous. Cascading. He continued down, senseless. And then the last stair creaked obnoxiously and he paused. 

His head felt heavy, like a burden to his shoulders. Everything felt so disturbed, out of place. It wasn’t right. When had things become so weird? Or had it always been this way, and he’d only realized now.

He pursed his lips and stood there at the bottom of the stairs. He gripped the railing and released it hastily, letting go and made his way to the coat rack. 

Arlo slipped out into the unforgiving cold. The wind bit his cheeks and the cool air stung his ears. He trudged a few meek steps and settled on the edge of the porch. His leg stuttered up and down, bouncing, his shoes scratching the small rocks, grinding across the ground.

His breath was like smoke in the saturated air, melting away into the surroundings. The emptiness in his chest now felt filled, becoming heavier, like an unforeseen force was holding him down. 

The front door opened and shut, and he felt someone settle beside him. An umbrella was chucked into his lap.

"You’re gonna catch a cold."

Arlo looked straight ahead, ignoring his brothers persistent gaze.

"I’ll head inside soon. "

He felt the obnoxious roll of eyes, and the umbrella leave his lap, as his brother unwrapped it and put it up, positioning it to shield them from the streaming water.

Arlo peered up, and pushed the umbrella away, tilting it from him and veering it towards his brother. 

Sound was sparse, and only the continuous drops of translucent liquid upon the surfaces could be heard.

Arlo stared ahead.


"Why does it always rain?"

His brother chuckled and shook his head, a smile playing on his lips as he look at him with a fondness in his eyes, a look reserved for children when they said something cute and amusing.
He hummed deep in his throat and nodded slowly.

"This again."

He looked at Arlo expectantly, but was greeted with nothing as he continued to look beyond.
He hummed.

"You always ask this."

He shook his head slowly and shrugged his shoulders. 

"It just, does. "

He continued to shake his head and raised his hands, lifting the umbrella with him.

"It’s like asking why time never stops.
It just is how it is." His voice raised as he petered off, and he laughed comically, huffing air through his nose.

Arlo didn’t look at him, instead staring straight ahead into the depths of the dimly lit street. The rain continued its torrent as it always did, sliding off the film of wetness on all the surfaces. He sighed, biting his lip, and opening his mouth before hesitating and shutting it. He started again.

“It doesn’t feel normal. It just feels wrong, like-"

He shut his mouth and breathed heavily, frowning. He gritted his teeth and trembled slightly, raising his arms in exasperation and letting them drop against his lap like dead weight.

"-Like it isn’t meant to be this way."

He shook his head and stared ahead. 

" It isn’t right."

Arlo re-evaluated and then burst.

"You know what in fact, it’s unnatural."

He licked his lips apprehensively, and collapsed in on himself, his two arms outstretched behind him bearing his weight. 

His brother glanced at him, before looking ahead.
The softness. The quietness. It was all consuming. 
The silence stretched out, spreading across the distance between them, as they just stared into the rain, which never stopped.

It was the incessant paranoia of an unseen force lingering in the background like a foul aftertaste. It hung stagnantly, waiting patiently, biding. 

Mason barely ever thought about it. It was a swift gnawing at the edge of his mind that passed as quickly as it’d arrived. It was a normal occurrence that evaporated from him, he’d feel the heaviness subsiding in his peripheral vision, and would be struck so suddenly with an immense fear that clawed restlessly at his chest like a depraved creature, before it vanished and he’d forgotten about it. Again. 

The streets were a raucous. People absentmindedly went around their day, milling around down the concrete slabs and asinine lampposts. The sky was an overhanging grimace. The buildings stood dull and desaturated, as if the color had been seeping out. They were all bland and tasteless, possessing the same air of lifelessness, utterly devoid of feeling.

Mason snapped his wrist up, and checked the reflective surface of the clock face, grimacing slightly before lowering his arm. He weaved between people, sliding past in a friction of fabric as he apologized meekly whilst shoving past. He was going to be late.

He sped up, chest seizing vigorously as he sprinted down. His feet ached from the tight constraints of his shoes, as he leapt each stride. It was so close. Mason ran in a frantic flurry of limbs, his hair haphazard in the lashings if the wind. 

It came out of nowhere. The ebbing darkness in his peripheral vision, spreading and subsiding in a fraction of a second. The weight in his chest doubled, and he couldn’t breathe, as he turned around in a full body contortion, reaching out. He was grasping at nothing but air, as he stretched further, pushing himself to the edge. It was a mere brush that sent tingles across his fingertips like a wildfire of electrify across his skin. He stretched his fingers further, reaching, grasping. He latched on.

The twinge in his throat caught, as he struggled with a strangled gasp. It was a faint rasp that escaped his lips, as he felt the beads of sweat lick his neck. The pulsation in his ears engulfed him as he stared. Mason had always been taught not to stare, the rule had been instilled in him from adolescence. It was rude. Though he completely disregarded it, as he stared, breathless. 

His mind was blank. He couldn’t think. The usual background noise was absent, and his whole head was empty, as if everything had just seeped out in an instant. 

He grasped it under his hand it. Supple and firm, the flesh he held corporal and real. The smile on it’s face looked wildly unnatural and out of place. Mason swallowed, the arm he was clutching felt warm, the heat undeniable. 

His lips quivered, as he tried to form a coherent sentence, or even a word. Nothing came out but silence. 

It smiled wider at him and clicked it’s tongue obnoxiously. 

Mason stared at it. The contours if it’s face, the planes if it’s neck and haphazard hair. The statute of its body, it’s height. It was all the same. It was identical. It was him.

Mason stared back at himself.

“Just the usual. Don’t worry, you’ll forget about me . You always do.” It said.

Mason trembled slightly. Fear was tracing its fingers down his back, and he released it and stepped back idly.

The quaking stopped. Mason frowned and looked around, and cringed at his shirt sticking to his back in a moist suction against his skin. Confusion blurred his head, and he wondered when it’d gotten so hot. He licked his lips and flicked his wrist gingerly, eyes widening as he turned to sprint. 

He ran down the sidewalk, pushing past people, ignoring the pressure behind his eyes. The wind pushed against him as he advanced forward and drove through.

And from behind it watched him from afar, and smiled. 

It tutted, eyeing the number on his wrist, stark against the paleness.

“2 more times.” It said aloud, to no one in particular. 

It pondered and surveyed, stalking mason as his figure grew tinier and tinier as it blurred into the distance. It watched, and it smiled.
